# ThrottleDeck

> Loopback-only, GET-only shared read-budget broker for Polymarket US and Kalshi,
> paired with a compact local Windows control window.

## Start here

- [Project README](README.md): Architecture, setup, active limits, failure
  contracts, caller policy, control window, and verification.
- [Documentation map](docs/README.md): Routes venue questions to the smallest
  relevant local or vendored source.
- [Caller adoption template](docs/ADOPTION-STATUS.md): Metrics-generated local
  status with explicit evidence limits and public-repository privacy guidance.
- [Detailed LLM context](llms-full.txt): Current service contracts and safe
  change boundaries.

## Source areas

- `venue_broker/`: Shared read broker on `127.0.0.1:8777`.
- `governor/`: Local control service and committed web bundle on
  `127.0.0.1:8778`.
- `ui/`: React/Vite source and browser tests.
- `broker_client.py`: Fail-closed client copied into adopting applications.
- `scripts/`: Setup, hidden Windows launchers, adoption update, and manual
  source-audit commands.
- `tests/`: Offline Python contracts and safety tests.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- The broker accepts GET only and has no order or fund-movement routes.
- Everything binds to loopback; no LAN or internet exposure.
- Callers never bypass an unavailable broker with a direct fallback.
- Credentials remain caller-owned and are forwarded only in memory.
- `/version` identifies the running build and `/callers` exposes the effective
  generic project/class/weight registry; both are local and upstream-free.
- The control window never becomes or supervises a second broker.
- Public configuration, docs, fixtures, and screenshots stay synthetic and
  contain no operator-specific application names or secrets.
- Do not hand-edit `docs/reference/`; it is vendored source material.
